steps.text: The solution's vapour pressure curve lies below that of the pure liquid solvent, and meets the (frozen solvent) curve at a lower temperature $T_f$ than the pure solvent's $T_f^\circ$.
Plot 1 shows the liquid solvent above the solution curve, both rising with temperature, with $\Delta T_f=T_f^\circ-T_f$ marked correctly.

pitfalls: Choosing a plot where the solution curve is above the solvent.

subject: chemistry
stem: Which of the following linear combination of atomic orbitals will lead to formation of molecular orbitals in homonuclear diatomic molecules [internuclear axis in $z$-direction]? A. $2p_z$ and $2p_x$ B. $2s$ and $2p_x$ C. $3d_{xy}$ and $3d_{x^2-y^2}$ D. $2s$ and $2p_z$ E. $2p_z$ and $3d_{x^2-y^2}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

steps.text: Orbitals combine only if they have non-zero net overlap, i.e. the same symmetry about the bond axis.
$2s$ and $2p_z$ both have $\sigma$ symmetry about $z$, so they overlap (D). The others have different symmetry and give zero overlap.

subject: chemistry
stem: $X$ g of benzoic acid on reaction with aq $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ released $\mathrm{CO_2}$ that occupied $11.2$ L volume at STP. $X$ is ______ g.

steps.text: $11.2$ L at STP is $0.5$ mol of $\mathrm{CO_2}$.
One mole of benzoic acid ($122$ g/mol) gives one mole of $\mathrm{CO_2}$, so $X=0.5\times122=61$ g.

subject: chemistry
stem: Consider the following reaction occurring in the blast furnace: $\mathrm{Fe_3O_{4(s)}}+4\mathrm{CO_{(g)}}\to3\mathrm{Fe_{(l)}}+4\mathrm{CO_{2(g)}}$. '$x$' kg of iron is produced when $2.32\times10^3$ kg $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$ and $2.8\times10^2$ kg CO are brought together in the furnace. The value of '$x$' is ______ (nearest integer). Given: molar mass of $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}=232$, CO $=28$, Fe $=56$ g/mol.

steps.text: $4$ kmol CO reacts with $1$ kmol $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$, so CO is limiting: $10$ kmol CO gives $\frac34\times10=7.5$ kmol Fe.

subject: chemistry
stem: $37.8$ g $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ was taken in a $1$ L reaction vessel and allowed to undergo the following reaction at $500$ K: $2\mathrm{N_2O_{5(g)}}\rightleftharpoons2\mathrm{N_2O_{4(g)}}+\mathrm{O_{2(g)}}$. The total pressure at equilibrium was found to be $18.65$ bar. Then, $K_p=$ ______ $\times10^{-2}$ [nearest integer]. Assume $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ to behave ideally under these conditions. Given: $R=0.082\ \mathrm{bar\,L\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$.

steps.text: Let $2x$ of $\mathrm{N_2O_5}$ react: pressures $14.35-2x$, $2x$ ($\mathrm{N_2O_4}$) and $x$ ($\mathrm{O_2}$). Total $=14.35+x=18.65$, so $x=4.3$.

pitfalls: Taking total pressure as the partial pressure of one gas.

subject: chemistry
stem: Among the following cations, the number of cations which will give characteristic precipitate in their identification tests with $\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$ is ______. $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}},\mathrm{Fe^{3+}},\mathrm{Ba^{2+}},\mathrm{Ca^{2+}},\mathrm{NH_4^+},\mathrm{Mg^{2+}},\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$

steps.text: $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ gives chocolate brown $\mathrm{Cu_2[Fe(CN)_6]}$, $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ gives Prussian blue, $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ gives white $\mathrm{Zn_2[Fe(CN)_6]}$.
$\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ and $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ are not identified this way in standard tests.

answer.source: official_final_key (numeric answer matched to question by value)

verification.note: Counting depends on the standard textbook tests (Cu, Fe(III), Zn); the answer $3$ matches the NTA numeric value.

subject: chemistry
stem: Standard entropies of $\mathrm{X_2}$, $\mathrm{Y_2}$ and $\mathrm{XY_5}$ are $70$, $50$ and $110\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}mol^{-1}}$ respectively. The temperature in Kelvin at which the reaction $\frac12\mathrm{X_2}+\frac52\mathrm{Y_2}\rightleftharpoons\mathrm{XY_5}$, $\Delta H^\theta=-35\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ will be at equilibrium is ______. (Nearest integer)

steps.text: At equilibrium $\Delta G=0$: $T=\frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}=\frac{-35000}{-50}=700$ K.

pitfalls: Unit mismatch between kJ and J.
